authority: This file is the ONLY place task status lives. BUILD-TRACKER.md defines tasks; it never records status.

status_values.todo: Not started. Eligible for selection when every `needs` id is `done`.
status_values.in_progress: Claimed by the current session. Only one task may hold this at a time.
status_values.done: Completed and verified. Its Verify commands passed.
status_values.blocked: Cannot be completed as written. `blocked_reason` is filled and the id is listed in `blocked_on`.
status_values.awaiting_human: Work an AI may not complete. Only a human may move this to `done`. Treated as NOT satisfying a dependency.
status_values.superseded: Replaced by a later task id. Never selected. Its output is not edited.

read_order_for_ai: 1. Read THIS file only (~10KB). Do not open ARCHITECTURE.md yet.
2. Check blocked_on. If non-empty, STOP and report to the user.
2b. Check `phase_gates`. If a gate's condition is not met, no task it guards may be selected, even if its `needs` are all done.

3. Find the first task in `tasks` with status 'todo' whose every `needs` id has status 'done'. That is the ONLY task for this session. A need with status 'awaiting_human', 'blocked' or 'superseded' does NOT count as satisfied. If no task qualifies and at least one task is 'awaiting_human', STOP and report: 'Build is waiting on human sign-off for <ids>. A human must set these to done in build-state.json before work continues.'
4. Open BUILD-TRACKER.md and read ONLY that task's card (search for its id).
5. Open ARCHITECTURE.md and read ONLY the sections listed in the card's `Load` line. Nothing else.
6. Build exactly the card's Do list. Touch only the card's Files.
7. Run the card's Verify commands. All must pass.
8. Update this file: set that task to 'done', append a session_log entry, bump updated_at.
9. STOP. Do not begin the next task, even if it looks trivial.
global_rules: ONE task per session. Never chain tasks.

Never revise a 'done' task's work. If a done task's output is wrong, add a new task with a new id and set the old one's status to 'superseded'. Additively extending a shared file (adding a script to package.json, adding a job to ci.yml, appending a section to docs/RUNBOOK.md) is NOT a revision and is allowed when that path appears in the current card's Files list.
Never invent facts about the school. See ARCHITECTURE.md A-3.1. Use the literal marker [[CONTENT REQUIRED — DO NOT PUBLISH]].
If a task cannot be completed as written, set status 'blocked', fill blocked_reason, add to blocked_on, and STOP.
If the work would need files outside the card's Files list, STOP and report scope drift instead of expanding.
Every completed task = one commit, message 'T-0XX: <title>'.
PRODUCT-SPEC.md assumes every decision in ARCHITECTURE.md Parts A/B. If a task's Load line names both and they disagree, ARCHITECTURE.md wins.

build-state.json `needs` is the only authoritative dependency graph. A card's `Needs` and `Unlocks` lines are a human-readable mirror; if they disagree with the JSON, the JSON wins and the card must be corrected.

M8_before_launch.rule: No task in M9 or M10 may be selected until every M8 task is done.

content_gate.rule: T-130 requires the ARCHITECTURE.md A-3.1 checklist signed off by the school. Placeholders must not reach production, which is what T-113's placeholder gate enforces.

human_gates.rule: T-131 is human-only. An AI sets it to 'awaiting_human' and never to 'done'. Only a human may set it to 'done', and that is what unblocks T-132.

No models added to schema.prisma; Prisma is mapped over this SQL in T-023. Admin screens are T-063, public pages T-083. Verified on a genuinely fresh database: created shifa_t014_verify, ran migrate deploy (all six migrations applied clean), exercised the constraints there, then dropped it and applied to shifa_dev with the non-destructive db:migrate. shifa_dev now holds 68 tables - 28 from T-010, 7 from T-011, 3 from T-012, 12 from T-013, these 17, and _prisma_migrations - and all seventeen new ones are empty. Constraint behaviour proved by transaction-and-rollback so nothing was seeded. Both of the card's Verify cases, each from both directions: a second is_current academic year is rejected whether created by UPDATE or by INSERT, while any number of non-current years coexist, so ux_academic_year_current is genuinely partial rather than a unique on a boolean; and a second current routine for the same class/section/year is rejected by ux_routine_current, while retiring the old one first (is_current=FALSE) or soft-deleting it frees the slot, and section B keeps its own independent slot. The COALESCE arm of that index was tested on its own: a class-wide routine with a NULL section occupies a distinct slot from section A's, and a second class-wide current routine is still rejected, because the NULLs collapse to 0 rather than each being distinct - which is exactly why the expression is there and not a plain three-column index. On the card's Contract: an information_schema sweep confirms no column named sections, section_count, no_of_sections or total_sections exists anywhere in the database, and sections behave as rows - A and B coexist for one class/year, the same name 'A' recurs in a different year, a duplicate name within one class/year is rejected, and capacity must be positive. Year scoping proved on the junction too: the same class+subject is rejected twice in one year but accepted in another. Subject master + junction proved by renaming: one UPDATE to subject_translations changed the name everywhere it appears, instead of PRD §5's fourteen edits. Also proved: RESTRICT protects class_grades, academic_years, subjects and routine media from deletion while still referenced; class_routines.media_id is NOT NULL, so a routine cannot exist as a bare URL; ends_on may be NULL or equal to starts_on but never earlier; an exam may carry no times but never ends_at before starts_at; exam term codes are unique per year and reusable across years; deleting a term cascades its exams while leaving class_grades intact. Pipeline green: prisma validate, tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest, next build. One integrity gap for T-022 and T-063, confirmed by experiment rather than inferred. class_routines.class_section_id has a plain FK to class_sections and nothing ties it to the routine's own class_grade_id and academic_year_id, so a routine for class_2 in 2025 can legally point at a section belonging to class_1 in 2026 - I inserted exactly that row and the database accepted it. The same shape of hole exists on exams: exams.subject_id references subjects directly, so a sitting can be scheduled for a subject that class_subjects never assigned to that class in that year. §B-8 is written this way and was transcribed rather than corrected; closing either one needs a composite unique key on the parent plus a composite FK, the same technique §B-4 already uses for user_module_permissions, and that belongs in T-022's constraint pass. Until then both are the admin UI's responsibility to prevent, and T-111 should cover them.

Faculty. prisma/migrations/0007_faculty/migration.sql transcribes ARCHITECTURE.md §B-7 table for table in the document's own order (faculty first, since the other four hang off it). Five tables - faculty, faculty_translations, faculty_private, faculty_subjects, faculty_class_assignments - with ck_faculty_photo_consent and the partial ix_faculty_public on sort_order WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status_code = 'published'. No models added to schema.prisma; Prisma is mapped over this SQL in T-023. Admin module with its consent gates is T-065, public page T-085. Verified on a genuinely fresh database: created shifa_t015_verify, ran migrate deploy (all seven migrations applied clean), exercised the constraints there, then dropped it and applied to shifa_dev with the non-destructive db:migrate. shifa_dev now holds 73 tables - 28 from T-010, 7 from T-011, 3 from T-012, 12 from T-013, 17 from T-014, these 5, and _prisma_migrations - and all five new ones are empty. Constraint behaviour proved by transaction-and-rollback so nothing was seeded. The card's Verify: setting photo_media_id with photo_consent_at NULL is rejected by ck_faculty_photo_consent, while a profile with no photo needs no photo consent and photo+consent together insert fine. One consequence of that CHECK worth knowing before T-065 builds the consent UI: it also blocks WITHDRAWAL. Clearing photo_consent_at on a row that still carries a photo fails, so a withdrawal has to null photo_consent_at and photo_media_id in the same statement. That is the right outcome - consent cannot silently lapse while the photo stays published - but a naive 'uncheck the consent box' form will hit a constraint error, so the admin action must clear both. On §A-16.2 requirement 6, physical separation: an information_schema sweep confirms the public faculty table carries no phone, email, address or emergency column at all, and that personal_phone, personal_email, emergency_contact and internal_notes exist in exactly one table in the whole database - faculty_private. A public profile read joins faculty to faculty_translations and structurally cannot reach a private column without naming the table. faculty_private is 1:1 by construction (the FK is the PK, so a second row for one member is rejected) and cascades away when the profile is deleted. On ADR-004: password_hash exists in exactly one table, users; faculty.user_id is an optional UNIQUE link, so two profiles cannot share a login, and deleting the user leaves the profile standing with the link nulled. Also proved: duplicate employee_code rejected; experience_years bounded 0..70; designation_id NOT NULL and RESTRICTed while referenced; status_code defaults to 'draft' and an unknown status fails the FK; one teacher holds two subjects (the many-to-many PRD §5's single string could not express), duplicates rejected, and deleting an assigned subject RESTRICTed; the Phase 2 faculty_class_assignments hook accepts a class-teacher row and cascades when the section is deleted. Pipeline green: prisma validate, tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest, next build. One gap for T-065 and T-113, confirmed by experiment. publish_consent_at is NOT enforced by the database: I set status_code='published' on a row with publish_consent_at NULL and it was accepted. §A-16.2 requirement 3 says a profile does not render without it and §B-7 gives the column no CHECK, so the photo half of consent is a database rule while the publish half is an application rule. Nothing in the schema stops a profile going public without consent - that has to be the write pipeline in T-065 and the consent gate in T-113, and it should be one of that gate's named cases rather than left implicit. A CHECK (status_code <> 'published' OR publish_consent_at IS NOT NULL) would close it, but adding one is a T-022 decision, not a revision of this migration.

Admission and fees. prisma/migrations/0008_admission/migration.sql transcribes ARCHITECTURE.md §B-9 table for table in the document's own order. 12 tables - admission_cycles(+tr), admission_steps(+tr), admission_documents(+tr), admission_eligibility(+tr), admission_faqs(+tr), fee_structures, fee_items - with ck_cycle_range, ck_age_range, the step_number and amount CHECKs, and ux_admission_cycle_current. No models added to schema.prisma; Prisma is mapped over this SQL in T-023. Admin module is T-064, public page T-084. Verified on a genuinely fresh database: created shifa_t016_verify, ran migrate deploy (all eight migrations applied clean), exercised the constraints there, then dropped it and applied to shifa_dev with the non-destructive db:migrate. shifa_dev now holds 85 tables - 28 from T-010, 7 from T-011, 3 from T-012, 12 from T-013, 17 from T-014, 5 from T-015, these 12, and _prisma_migrations - and all twelve new ones are empty. Constraint behaviour proved by transaction-and-rollback so nothing was seeded. Both of the card's Verify cases: a duplicate (fee_structure_id, fee_type_id) is rejected by fee_items_fee_structure_id_fee_type_id_key, and a second fee structure for the same class and year is rejected by fee_structures_class_grade_id_academic_year_id_key, while the same class in another year and another class in the same year both insert - so the uniqueness is on the pair, not on either column. On the card's Contract, checked against the live catalogue rather than by reading the file back: fee_items has exactly four columns - id, fee_structure_id, fee_type_id, amount - so there is no recurrence and no ordering on it; and is_recurring_monthly and is_one_time exist in exactly one table in the database, fee_types. The 2NF payoff was demonstrated rather than asserted: flipping 'is tuition monthly?' was a single UPDATE on fee_types and took effect for every structure referencing it, where a column on fee_items would have needed one edit per class per year and could have disagreed between rows. Also on fees: three charges coexist as rows for one structure, which is what PRD §5's single otherCharges column could not express; amount is NUMERIC(12,2) and sums; a negative amount is rejected but zero is accepted, which matters because a waived charge is legitimate and must be expressible; deleting a structure cascades its items, while fee_types and class_grades are RESTRICTed while referenced. On admission: one cycle per academic year and one is_current cycle overall, both enforced, with a non-current cycle for another year accepted; ck_cycle_range rejects closes_on before opens_on but allows either or both to be NULL, so an open-ended cycle is expressible; step_number must be positive, step titles are NOT NULL per locale, reordering is an UPDATE, and a step with a NULL cycle is evergreen - deleting the cycle cascades its own steps away and leaves the evergreen one standing, which is the behaviour the NULL is for. Eligibility is genuinely structured: min/max ages are NUMERIC so 5.5 years is expressible, ck_age_range rejects max below min, an open-ended range is allowed, and one row per class is enforced. FAQ question and answer are both NOT NULL. Pipeline green: prisma validate, tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest, next build. One note for T-064 and T-022. admission_cycles.is_open and ux_admission_cycle_current are independent: nothing prevents the current cycle from having is_open = FALSE, or a non-current cycle from having is_open = TRUE. Both are legitimate states - a cycle can be current but not yet open - but it does mean 'is admission open right now' has to be read as an explicit combination rather than from either flag alone, and the public page in T-084 and the admin toggle in T-064 must agree on which expression that is. §B-9 defines no such expression the way §B-11 does for notices, so it is worth naming one before two screens invent different answers.

Home and about content. prisma/migrations/0009_home_about/migration.sql transcribes ARCHITECTURE.md §B-10 table for table in the document's own order, which also satisfies the FK dependencies (each parent before its translations). 12 tables - hero_slides(+tr), home_content(+tr), features(+tr), about_content(+tr), committee_members(+tr), achievements(+tr) - with the CHECK (id = 1) guard on both singletons and the achieved_year range CHECK. No models added to schema.prisma; Prisma is mapped over this SQL in T-023. Admin modules are T-061 and T-062, public pages T-081 and T-082. Verified on a genuinely fresh database: created shifa_t017_verify, ran migrate deploy (all nine migrations applied clean), exercised the constraints there, then dropped it and applied to shifa_dev with the non-destructive db:migrate. shifa_dev now holds 97 tables - 28 from T-010, 7 from T-011, 3 from T-012, 12 from T-013, 17 from T-014, 5 from T-015, 12 from T-016, these 12, and _prisma_migrations - and all twelve new ones are empty. Constraint behaviour proved by transaction-and-rollback so nothing was seeded. The card's Verify, on both singletons and from every direction: a bare INSERT lands on id = 1 (cta_url defaulting to '/admission'); id = 2 is rejected by the CHECK; a second row re-using id = 1 is rejected by the primary key; id = 0 and id = -1 are rejected too, so the guard is not just 'no second row' but 'exactly the row numbered 1'; and the CHECK holds on UPDATE as well, so an existing singleton cannot be renumbered out of the way to make room for another. Also proved: both locales hang off the one home_content row as separate translation rows and a duplicate (id, locale) is rejected by the composite PK; deleting a singleton cascades its translations away; an unknown locale fails the FK, renaming a locale cascades into the 0009 translation tables, and deleting one still referenced is refused (the FKs carry ON UPDATE CASCADE and no ON DELETE clause, so NO ACTION). On the repeating content: hero_slides.media_id is NOT NULL and RESTRICTed, so a slide cannot exist without an image and the image cannot be deleted out from under it, while features/committee/achievements media is SET NULL, so deleting an illustrative image keeps the row; three slides coexist with their own sort_order and their own per-locale title, which is the point of rows over numbered columns; feature/achievement title and committee name+designation are NOT NULL per locale; deleting a parent cascades its translations; deleting the user recorded in deleted_by_user_id keeps the row and nulls the attribution; achieved_year accepts 1900, 2200 and NULL but rejects 1899 and 2201. Pipeline green: prisma validate, tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest, next build. Two gaps for later, both confirmed by experiment rather than inferred. First, committee_members.publish_consent_at is not enforced by the database: I inserted an is_active member carrying a photo with publish_consent_at NULL and it was accepted. These are named individuals with photographs, exactly what §A-16.2 covers, and faculty has ck_faculty_photo_consent for the photo half - committee members have no equivalent, so both halves are application rules. T-062's write pipeline and T-113's consent gate must cover it, and T-113 should name committee members as a case of its own rather than assume the faculty gate reaches them. A CHECK mirroring ck_faculty_photo_consent would close the photo half, but adding one is a T-022 decision, not a revision of this migration. Second, hero_slides.starts_at/ends_at have no range CHECK - I inserted a slide whose window ends a day before it starts and the database accepted it. §B-8 and §B-9 both guard their date pairs (ck_event_range, ck_cycle_range) and §B-10 does not, so the omission is visible against its own neighbours; an inverted window silently means 'never shows', with no error for the editor. That is the T-061 form's job to reject until T-022 decides whether to add ck_slide_range.

Notices. prisma/migrations/0010_notices/migration.sql transcribes ARCHITECTURE.md §B-11 table for table in the document's own order, which also satisfies the FK dependencies (notices first, since the other three hang off it). Four tables - notices, notice_translations, notice_attachments, notice_attachment_translations - with ck_notice_published and the partial ix_notices_public on published_at DESC WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status_code = 'published' (pg_indexes confirms the WHERE clause is on the index, not just in a query). No models added to schema.prisma; Prisma is mapped over this SQL in T-023. Admin module with its publish action is T-066, public list and detail T-086. Verified on a genuinely fresh database: created shifa_t018_verify, ran migrate deploy (all ten migrations applied clean), exercised the constraints there, then dropped it and applied to shifa_dev with the non-destructive db:migrate. shifa_dev now holds 101 tables - 28 from T-010, 7 from T-011, 3 from T-012, 12 from T-013, 17 from T-014, 5 from T-015, 12 from T-016, 12 from T-017, these 4, and _prisma_migrations - and all four new ones are empty. Constraint behaviour proved by transaction-and-rollback so nothing was seeded. Both of the card's Verify cases, each from every direction. ck_notice_published rejects status_code='published' with published_at NULL on INSERT, rejects the same state reached by UPDATE (publishing a draft without setting a time), and rejects clearing published_at on an already-published notice - so a published row can never lose its timestamp, which is what closes AUDIT D-2. A draft with no time is accepted, and publishing with a time succeeds. And the per-locale slug: two different notices cannot share (locale_code, slug), while the same slug string is free in the other locale and the two locales may carry entirely different slugs - which is the reason slug lives on the translation rather than on notices, since one shared slug would force a Bangla notice under an English path or the reverse. Also proved: a second translation of one notice in the same locale is rejected by the composite PK; title and body_html are NOT NULL while excerpt is optional. On the card's Contract, the visibility expression was tested as an expression rather than asserted. Five notices - live, scheduled, soft-deleted, draft, archived - were inserted and status_code='published' AND published_at <= now() AND deleted_at IS NULL selected exactly one, with each arm rejecting a different row. A future published_at is accepted and simply not yet visible, so scheduled publishing falls out of the same expression and is deliberately not constrained; ix_notices_public carries the two immutable arms and omits the time test, which cannot be indexed because now() is not immutable. The index was shown to be genuinely partial: 100 rows in the table, 50 matching its predicate. On attachments: three files sit on one notice with their own sort_order and per-locale label - the shape PRD §5's single attachment could not express - a file may be attached to two different notices since uniqueness is on the (notice, media) pair, the same file twice on one notice is rejected, label is NOT NULL, and media_assets is RESTRICTed while attached so a file cannot vanish from under a published notice. Deleting a notice cascades its translations, its attachments and their labels while leaving the media rows standing; the category is RESTRICTed while referenced; unknown status_code and unknown category id both fail their FKs; author, publisher and deleter attribution is SET NULL, so deleting a user keeps the notice; and both ON UPDATE CASCADE paths work - renaming a content_status carries into notices.status_code, renaming a locale carries into notice_translations. Pipeline green: prisma validate, tsc --noEmit, eslint, vitest, next build. One note for T-066 and T-086. is_pinned is independent of visibility - a pinned draft, a pinned scheduled notice and a pinned soft-deleted notice are all accepted, and §B-11 defines no expression combining the two the way it does for visibility. That is correct as data (pinning a notice before it goes live is legitimate), but it means the homepage strip and the list ordering must apply the visibility expression FIRST and only then order by is_pinned DESC, published_at DESC. If either screen orders by is_pinned before filtering, a pinned draft leads the list. Worth naming that composite ordering once, in T-086, rather than letting the list page and the homepage strip each invent it - the same class of drift the visibility expression was made a single definition to avoid.
